question: One side of a parallelogram drawn from a vertex is represented by $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$, while the diagonal through that vertex is $5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$. Find the vector representing the other adjacent side and verify the diagonal relation.
explanation:
Step 1: Parallelogram addition relation
If the adjacent-side vectors are $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ and the diagonal is $\vec{d}$, then
\(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=\vec{d}\)
Step 2: Isolation of the unknown side
\(\vec{b}=\vec{d}-\vec{a}\)
Substituting the given vectors,
\(\vec{b}=(5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k})-(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k})\)
Step 3: Simplification
\(\vec{b}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\)
Step 4: Verification
\(\vec{a}+\vec{b}=(2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k})+(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-3\hat{k})=5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
Final Answer
The other adjacent side is $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$.

options.A: The other adjacent side is $3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}-3\hat{k}$, and adding it to $2\hat{i}-3\hat{j}+\hat{k}$ gives $5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$.
options.B: The other adjacent side is $7\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-\hat{k}$, and the diagonal is their difference.
options.D: The other adjacent side is $5\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}$ because the diagonal equals either adjacent side.
